title: Data Ingestion
tagline: The answer is not in the system yet. Get it in, keep it true, and know when it is wrong.
story: The question has crossed the model and the cache, and it needs knowledge the system does not hold yet. Files sit in storage, rows change in a database, pages live in a library with permissions, and some of it is scanned paper. Ingestion decides what the assistant can ever know, how stale it is, and whether a deleted or restricted document keeps answering. This world is the choice of pipeline and the discipline of keeping the index equal to the source.
oneLiner: Choose how content gets in, parse it faithfully, keep it fresh, repeatable and deletable, and gate what enters the index.
youWillLearn: Pick an ingestion architecture (indexer, push, event-driven, batch) from source mix, freshness and team size
Choose a parser by document type, volume and residency, and represent tables and figures so they stay answerable
Detect changes and deletes per source, and say what each indexer and change feed cannot see
Make writes idempotent with stable ids and content hashes so retries and replays are safe
Re-embed with zero downtime using a new index behind an alias, with a rollback window
Design dead-letter, retry and backpressure paths, and gate PII and permissions at ingest
Know which Azure AI Search ingestion features are GA and which are preview as of 2026-10-13

flashcards.front: What are the smallest and longest Azure AI Search indexer schedule intervals?
flashcards.back: 5 minutes to 1,440 minutes (24 hours), set as an XSD duration such as `PT2H`. For seconds of freshness, push from an event pipeline instead of scheduling an indexer.

flashcards.front: What are the push indexing batch limits and the meaning of HTTP 207 and 503?
flashcards.back: At most 1,000 documents or 16 MB per request (HTTP 413 above). 207 means partial failure, so check each document. 503 means wait and retry.

flashcards.front: Why is `mergeOrUpload` the usual push action, and why is replay safe?
flashcards.back: It upserts by key, so a replayed batch overwrites instead of duplicating. `delete` of a key that is not in the index is also safe.

flashcards.front: What do the Blob and Cosmos DB indexers do with hard deletes?
flashcards.back: They never see them. You need a soft-delete policy from the first run (native blob soft delete, or a flag such as `IsDeleted=true`), or a reconciliation job.

flashcards.front: Which Azure SQL change detection policy sees deleted rows?
flashcards.back: `SqlIntegratedChangeTrackingPolicy`, for tables only. `HighWaterMarkChangeDetectionPolicy` (rowversion or updated column) also works for views, and deletes then need a soft-delete column policy.

flashcards.front: What does the Cosmos DB change feed in latest version mode miss?
flashcards.back: Deletes, and every intermediate update: it keeps only the latest create or update per item. All versions and deletes mode records everything but needs continuous backup and reads only within that window.

flashcards.front: Event Grid and Debezium both deliver at least once. What follows?
flashcards.back: Duplicates will happen after faults, so the sink must be idempotent: stable keys, upserts and a hash check. Exactly-once effect comes from the write, not the pipe.

flashcards.front: How do you fire a blob event only after a block blob is fully committed?
flashcards.back: Filter `BlobCreated` on the `CopyBlob`, `PutBlob`, `PutBlockList` or `FlushWithClose` API calls, so a worker never reads a half-written blob.

flashcards.front: Why does a restored blob or a renamed ADLS Gen2 directory stay out of the index?
flashcards.back: Change detection reads the blob `LastModified` timestamp, and neither a restore nor a directory rename changes it. Touch the blob or reset the document or indexer.

flashcards.front: What are the PII Detection skill defaults, and how do you mask?
flashcards.back: `maskingMode` defaults to `none` and `minimumPrecision` to 0.0. Set `maskingMode: replace` to get `maskedText`. Run it before embedding if PII must not reach the index.

flashcards.front: What must projections copy so ACLs can be enforced at query time?
flashcards.back: The ACL fields (for example `metadata_user_ids`, `metadata_group_ids`) onto every chunk. Knowledge source `ingestionPermissionOptions` needs `2026-08-01-preview`, not `2026-04-01`.

flashcards.front: How do you re-embed a corpus with zero downtime?
flashcards.back: Build a new index with the new model beside the old one, validate it, repoint the index alias, and keep the old index for a rollback window. Embedding models cannot be upgraded in place.

flashcards.front: What does `maxFailedItems: -1` do and why is it risky?
flashcards.back: The indexer keeps going however many documents fail. Poison documents then vanish quietly, so watch error counts and keep a dead-letter list.

flashcards.front: What is the Document Layout skill timeout and billing quirk?
flashcards.back: Documents that need over 5 minutes in the layout model time out, and are still charged when a Foundry resource is attached. Split very large files first.

flashcards.front: What changed in Document Intelligence layout v4.0 (2024-11-30) that breaks old parsers?
flashcards.back: Tables come out as HTML tables, and selection marks are the characters ☒ and ☐ instead of `:selected:` and `:unselected:`. Re-run your parsing tests on upgrade.

flashcards.front: When does a vision LLM beat OCR or layout analysis, and what does it cost?
flashcards.back: On charts and visual pages where the meaning is in the picture. It costs tokens per page, is not deterministic, and can drop or invent cells, so validate on a labelled set.

flashcards.front: Why do child chunk keys from index projections replace stale chunks, and what do deletes need?
flashcards.back: Projected keys contain a hash that changes when the parent changes. Children of a deleted parent go only if the data source has a deletion detection policy.

glossary.def: An Azure AI Search crawler that pulls from a supported data source on a schedule, detects changes and can run a skillset on the way into an index.
The enrichment pipeline an indexer runs per document: parse, OCR, split, embed or call a custom skill.
Your code sends documents to the index with the Index Documents API (`upload`, `merge`, `mergeOrUpload`, `delete`). You own parsing, chunking and embedding.
Reading inserts, updates and deletes from a database log or change feed so downstream systems receive each change instead of rescanning the table.
A write that gives the same result when repeated. With stable keys and `mergeOrUpload`, a replayed batch overwrites rather than duplicates.
A digest of a document or chunk's text, stored beside it. If the hash is unchanged, skip parsing, embedding and writing.
Marking a document as deleted (a flag or the storage service's own soft delete) so an indexer can see the delete, then removing it from the index.
A record that says an item was deleted. Change streams emit tombstones so consumers can remove the item downstream.
A holding place for messages or documents that failed after retries, kept with the failure reason so they can be inspected and replayed.
A signal or limit that slows producers when a consumer or downstream API (such as an embedding endpoint) cannot keep up.
A service-level secondary name for an index. Repointing it moves traffic to a rebuilt index with no application change.
Run the old (blue) and new (green) index side by side, validate green, switch the alias, and keep blue for rollback.
A skillset feature that writes one index document per chunk (one to many) with a parent key, so chunks can be filtered and replaced by parent.
A parsing model that returns reading order, tables, headings, figures and page coordinates, not only a text stream.
An Azure service that analyses documents, images, audio and video into schema-defined fields with confidence scores, also exposed as an AI Search skill.
An AI Search skill that finds personal data in text and can return a masked copy before the text is embedded.

claims.text: The smallest Azure AI Search indexer schedule interval is 5 minutes and the longest is 1,440 minutes (24 hours).
A push indexing request carries at most 1,000 documents or 16 MB, HTTP 413 is returned above that, 207 means partial failure and 503 means wait and retry.
mergeOrUpload is the usual push action for incremental updates, and delete on a key that is not in the index is safe, so a replayed batch is safe.

GA indexer data sources are Blob Storage (ADLS Gen2 through the blob indexer), Cosmos DB for NoSQL, Azure SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, Table Storage and OneLake, while SharePoint in Microsoft 365, Azure MySQL and Cosmos DB for MongoDB are preview.
Foundry IQ indexed knowledge source kinds for a search index, Azure Blob and OneLake carry no preview label, while Azure SQL, File and Indexed SharePoint kinds are preview.
Plan for indexer runs of about 2 hours; the limits page lists 2 or 24 hours depending on tier and environment.
An indexer run is reported as Success even when individual documents fail, as long as the number of errors stays below the Max failed items setting.
Blob Storage events through Event Grid and Debezium change events are both delivered at least once, so duplicates can occur.
Document Intelligence layout v4.0 (2024-11-30, GA) renders tables as HTML tables and selection marks as the characters ☒ and ☐ instead of :selected: and :unselected:.
In the Document Layout skill, documents that need over 5 minutes in the layout model time out, and are still charged when a Foundry resource is attached.
Content Understanding API 2025-11-01 is GA, and 2026-06-01-preview adds signature detection and document metadata extraction.
The Content Understanding skill is GA in search REST 2026-04-01, while semantic chunking and AI image descriptions are preview (2026-05-01-preview).
Docling has an MIT-licensed codebase, can run locally for sensitive or air-gapped data, and its latest release at the check date was v2.138.0 (2026-10-12).
Document Intelligence S0 limits are 500 MB and 2,000 pages per file, and the F0 tier allows 4 MB and 2 pages.
Content Understanding asynchronous document analysis allows 200 MB and 300 pages for PDF and images.

The blob indexer detects changes through the LastModified timestamp, does not track deletes by default, and does not re-index a restored soft-deleted blob or a renamed ADLS Gen2 directory because LastModified does not change.
SqlIntegratedChangeTrackingPolicy works for tables only and detects deleted rows, while HighWaterMarkChangeDetectionPolicy on a rowversion or updated column also works for views.
The Cosmos DB for NoSQL indexer uses a high water mark on _ts, needs a top-level Boolean soft-delete field for delete detection, and never sees hard deletes.

The Cosmos DB change feed in latest version mode records creates and updates only (the latest change per item) and not deletes, while all versions and deletes mode needs continuous backup and can be read only within the backup retention window.
Items in one Cosmos DB transactional batch share a modification time and may arrive in any order in the change feed.
Index projection child keys contain a hash that changes when the parent changes, and children of a deleted parent are removed only if the data source has a deletion detection policy.
Reset Documents, Reset Skills and Resync are preview APIs in 2026-08-01-preview, while Reset Indexer is the GA full reset.
An index alias is a service-level resource that can be repointed to a rebuilt index, and the Serverless Developer tier does not support aliases.
Azure embedding models cannot be upgraded in place and an embeddings call accepts up to 2,048 input items.
The PII Detection skill has minimumPrecision (0.0 to 1.0, default 0.0), maskingMode (default none, replace returns maskedText), maskingCharacter, domain and piiCategories parameters.

Knowledge source ingestionPermissionOptions requires 2026-08-01-preview and is not supported in 2026-04-01, and index projection mappings must copy ACL fields such as metadata_user_ids and metadata_group_ids onto every chunk.
The indexer properties maxFailedItems and maxFailedItemsPerBatch accept a positive integer, and -1 continues no matter how many errors occur.
The SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer is preview, user-delegated tokens expire every 75 minutes, and password-protected and user-encrypted files are not supported.
